database_memories: ENSURE: When retrieving previous non-zero volume and computing daily_change in the parsed data, use parsed_date (integer) rather than market_date (string) in both the predicates and ORDER BY
| CONTEXT: The parsed CTE (or underlying table) exposes market_date as a VARCHAR and parsed_date as an integer YYYYMMDD; string ordering on market_date causes lexicographical misordering of dates
| WHEN_TO_CHECK: In correlated subqueries that join the table to itself (e.g., p2.previous_volume lookup)
ENSURE: Apply date-range filters on parsed_date instead of using SUBSTR(market_date) to correctly bound the query
| CONTEXT: Filtering on SUBSTR(market_date) risks lexicographical anomalies and can omit intended rows
| WHEN_TO_CHECK: In the WHERE clause of the final SELECT against the parsed CTE or base market data table
generic_memories: VERIFY: Consistency of columns in predicates and ORDER BY within correlated subqueries
| PRINCIPLE: Using different columns or data types for filtering versus ordering can fetch the wrong “previous” or “next” record
| WHEN_TO_APPLY: Whenever writing a correlated subquery or APPLY clause to retrieve a related row based on ordering
ENSURE: Date comparisons and ordering use true date or integer representations, not raw string columns
| PRINCIPLE: Lexicographical sorting of string-formatted dates can misorder days and months (e.g., "2021-8-10" may come before "2021-08-2")
| WHEN_TO_APPLY: When filtering, joining, or ordering data by date values stored as strings
– Right: ORDER BY CAST(date_string AS DATE)
